name: Acrobatics
description: Your Dexterity check covers your attempt to stay on your feet in a tricky situation, such as when you're trying to run across a sheet of ice, balance on a tightrope, or stay upright on a rocking ship's deck. The GM might also decide that a DEX check other than Acrobatics is appropriate when you try to accomplish a task that relies heavily on balance.

name: Animal Handling
description: When there is any question whether you can calm down a domesticated animal, keep a mount from getting spooked, or intuit an animal's intentions, the GM might ask for a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check. You also make a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check to control your mount when you attempt a risky maneuver.

name: Arcana
description: Your Intelligence check measures your ability to recall lore about spells, magic items, eldritch symbols, magical traditions, the planes of existence, and the inhabitants of those planes. These checks represent knowledge gleaned through study and memorization of various things relating to magic.

name: Athletics
description: Your Strength check covers difficult situations you encounter while climbing, jumping, or swimming. Each of these activities can also involve a Constitution check, at the GM's option, if the task involves extended physical exertion.

name: Deception
description: Your Charisma check determines whether you can convincingly hide the truth, either verbally or through your actions. This deception can encompass everything from misleading others through ambiguity to telling outright lies.

name: History
description: Your Intelligence check measures your ability to recall lore about historical events, legendary people, ancient kingdoms, past disputes, recent wars, and lost civilizations.

name: Insight
description: Your Wisdom check decides whether you can discern true intentions from a creature's behavior, speech, and mannerisms. You attempt to determine if someone is lying when they're really trying to seem honest.

name: Intimidation
description: When you attempt to influence someone through overt threats, hostile actions, and physical violence, the GM might ask you to make a Charisma (Intimidation) check. Examples include trying to pry information out of a prisoner, convincing street thugs to back down, or using the edge of a broken bottle to convince an uncooperative tavern owner to lend you some coin.

name: Investigation
description: When you look around for clues and make deductions based on those clues, you make an Intelligence (Investigation) check. You might deduce the location of a hidden object, discern from the appearance of a wound what kind of weapon dealt it, or determine the weakest point in a tunnel that could cause it to collapse.

name: Medicine
description: A Wisdom (Medicine) check lets you try to stabilize a dying companion or diagnose an illness. You attempt to diagnose an illness when someone can spend more than just a few minutes with the patient.

name: Nature
description: Your Intelligence check measures your ability to recall lore about terrain, plants and animals, the weather, and natural cycles.

name: Perception
description: Your Wisdom (Perception) check lets you spot, hear, or otherwise detect the presence of something. It measures your awareness of your surroundings by the use of your senses.

name: Performance
description: Your Charisma (Performance) check determines how well you can delight an audience with music, dance, acting, storytelling, or some other form of entertainment.

name: Persuasion
description: When you attempt to influence someone or a group of people with tact, social graces, or good nature, the GM might ask you to make a Charisma (Persuasion) check. Typically, you're trying to persuade someone to do something or to agree with your point of view.

name: Religion
description: Your Intelligence check measures your ability to recall lore about deities, rites and prayers, religious hierarchies, holy symbols, and the practices of secret cults.

name: Sleight of Hand
description: Whenever you attempt an act of legerdemain or manual trickery, such as planting something on someone else or concealing an object on your person, make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The GM might also call for a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check to determine whether you successfully lift a coin purse off another person or slip something out of another person's pocket.

name: Stealth
description: Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check when you attempt to hide from an enemy, slink past guards, slip away without being noticed, or sneak up on someone. You might try to hide in shadows or among tall grass with a cloak that is mottled with colors to match the environment.

name: Survival
description: The GM might ask you to make a Wisdom (Survival) check to follow tracks, hunt wild game, guide your group through frozen wastelands, identify signs that owlbears are nearby, predict the weather, or avoid quicksand and other natural hazards.
